source: AISC Design Guide 1, 2nd ed., Sect. 3.4 printed text and equations (Fig. 3.4.1 page through Sect. 3.5.2)
why_this_exists: Resolves the tension-lever-arm question opened by dg1_example_4_7_large_moment.json. The module's x and Example 4.7's x disagreed; this is the equation that decides between them.

equations_verbatim.3.3.15a: t_p(req) = 2.11*sqrt( f_p(max)*Y*(m - Y/2) / Fy )   (LRFD, if Y < m)
equations_verbatim.3.3.15_note: When n is larger than m, the thickness will be governed by n. Substitute n for m in Equations 3.3.14 and 3.3.15.
equations_verbatim.3.4.5a: M_pl = Tu*x/B   (LRFD)   -- per unit width, NO factor of 1/2
equations_verbatim.3.4.6_prose: The tension force Tu (LRFD) in the anchor rods will cause bending in the base plate. Cantilever action is conservatively assumed with the span length equal to the distance from the rod centerline to the CENTER OF THE COLUMN FLANGE, x.

3.4.6_symbols.d: depth of wide flange column section

equations_verbatim.3.4.2_sect: For the case of large moments, the bearing stress is at its limiting value: f_p = f_p(max)

3.4.3.module: Y = half - sqrt(half**2 - 2*M_net/q_max), half = f + N/2

3.3.14.module: t = l_cant*sqrt(2*f_p/(0.9*Fy)); coefficient sqrt(2/0.9) = 1.4907 where DG 1 prints 1.5

3.3.15.module: t = sqrt(4*f_p*Y*(l_cant - Y/2)/(0.9*Fy)); coefficient 2/sqrt(0.9) = 2.108 where DG 1 prints 2.11

3.3.15_note.match: exact - the note's substitution is built in

3.4.6.module: x_arm = f - d/2 + tf/2 when tf is given

resolution_of_the_open_question.was_open: Example 4.7 uses x = N/2 - d/2 - 1.5 = f - d/2 = 2.15 in., with no tf/2. The module uses x = f - d/2 + tf/2 = 2.60 in.
resolution_of_the_open_question.now_closed: Eq. 3.4.6 reads x = f - d/2 + tf/2, and the prose states the span is measured to the CENTER OF THE COLUMN FLANGE. The module conforms to the governing equation. Example 4.7 measures to the OUTER FACE of the flange and is short by tf/2 = 0.45 in.
resolution_of_the_open_question.verdict: MODULE CORRECT. The tf/2 term stays. The warning issued when tf is omitted is correct as written: omitting it is unconservative against Eq. 3.4.6.
resolution_of_the_open_question.outcome: The module's tension-interface thickness for Example 4.7 is 1.706 in. against the example's 1.44 in. Neither governs there (bearing asks 1.90 in.), so the example's final plate is unaffected.

errors_now_confirmed_in_example_4_7: Substitutes f = 9.5 in. into Eqs. 3.4.3 and 3.4.4 after computing f = 8.5 in. for the same 20x20 plate. Y and T are consequently low: 12.0 / 156 kips printed against 12.606 / 181.19 kips from the example's own stated geometry. Rod demand becomes 60.4 kips/rod against the 57.7 kips it cites.
Takes x = f - d/2, omitting the tf/2 of Eq. 3.4.6. Understates the tension-interface thickness by sqrt(1 + tf/(2*(f - d/2))) = 10% here.
note_on_closing: These four flags were already True, closed 2026-08-31 against this same document. This record is the second, independent transcription of Sect. 3.4 and it agrees with the first line for line. It does not close anything new.
